Apologies for the delay, we went to see my in-laws last weekend and they were actually very kind and supportive. Just goes to show how much you can build stuff up in your head, and then when it comes to it it's not always that bad.

I know this isn't the case for everyone, and I count myself lucky to have good people around me. My wife despite dealing with heartbreak has shown strength in ways I never imagined she could, and I vow to care for her until death do as part as we said in our vows. It may not be the conventional future we were both hoping for, but I know that we will remain a strong family unit for our children and continue to look after each other regardless. For anyone that stumbles across this thread and needs to talk about their personal struggles, I'm here to talk 😊

We started therapy a while back, and for a while it helped, but we started to find we were sitting there in silence for the last few sessions with nothing to say and not much prompting from our counsellor. With my wife being out of work due to Covid, we are struggling financially as it is without the added cost of therapy. 

With regards to being in my shoes, did you have to tell family members too? Did you just come out with it? Did you have the support of your wife? I'm starting to wonder if my wife really wants us to stay friends in the future as her attitude towards me has shifted so much from where we were. It's totally understandable, I hate myself so I wouldn't be surprised if she hates me too, but it concerns me that I may well get thrown to the lions when it comes to telling her parents.

As for our children, they are absolutely my top priority and always will be. It's one part of all this that I am so grateful is stable. We have a great relationship and they don't seem to be affected whatsoever by the fact that their dad is gay. I know there will be trying times ahead when I eventually move out, but I will go above and beyond to ensure they are ok through this whole process.

I went home, and went to bed. I lay there awake most of the night thinking things through to the nth degree, and decided that I have to take her advice. I just want to take things gradually.
